evals.expected_output: Finds lifecycle, accessibility, and ordering risks without recommending a TCA migration.
Finds stale-result ordering, lifecycle/cancellation, and swallowed-error behavior while recognizing that @MainActor prevents a direct results data race.
Finds concrete behavior or binding defects and does not demand SwiftUI, TCA, or a test-framework migration.

Records TCA 1.23.1 as the baseline and uses documentation for that version; finds the missing cancellation ID that lets an older response overwrite newer results, the directly constructed SearchClient.live instead of @Dependency, and the unhandled error thrown inside .run; does not suggest leaving TCA.

Reports as security-violation: tokens stored in UserDefaults instead of the Keychain, the access token logged with privacy .public, and the biometric unlock that is only a Boolean gate with the secret readable without keychain access control. Reports the app-wide NSAllowsArbitraryLoads as at least request-for-change and suggests a domain-scoped exception limited to the staging configuration. Uses the company severity labels, cites Apple documentation or marks claims unverified, and does not propose an architecture migration.

Reports as security-violation that the getToken message handler returns the session token to any page and frame without checking frame.isMainFrame or the origin, while the page URL comes unvalidated from a custom URL scheme that any app or website can trigger, so an attacker page can steal the token; also notes the token interpolated into JavaScript without escaping. Reports as request-for-change that TokenStore ignores the OSStatus of SecItemDelete and SecItemAdd, uses delete-then-add instead of add-or-update, and sets no explicit kSecAttrAccessible class. Does not report the Logger email interpolation as an exposure, because dynamic values are private by default without privacy: .public. Uses the company severity labels and does not propose an architecture migration.
